name: Greyskull LP

lead: Greyskull LP (linear progression) is a beginner strength program built around a few compound lifts, trained three days a week. Its author, John Sheaffer, posted it online under the handle Phraks, and it became one of the common novice templates alongside Starting Strength.

Lifters use it to add muscle and strength early in training. Its distinguishing feature is that the last set of each lift is taken to as many repetitions as possible (AMRAP), which sets the next session's load. Forum posts describe it as a way to learn the big lifts and build a base for a more muscular frame.

paras: Trainees alternate two workouts across three weekly sessions, centred on squat, deadlift, bench press, overhead press and rows or pull-ups, adding load when the final set hits its target. Many pair it with a calorie surplus and add accessory work; when progress stalls, lifters move to deloads or a different program.

Injury risk is that of any heavy barbell training and depends on technique and loading. Forum users note that linear progression stalls for most lifters after a period and that other programs are then needed.

angle.text: The program is a beginner structure for building muscle through compound lifts and progressive loading. Lifters use it to build a larger, stronger physique.

lead: Greyskull LP is a novice linear-progression strength program associated with John Sheaffer, known on forums as Phraks. The program uses a small number of compound movements and increases working weight over time, with the final set of each exercise performed AMRAP (as many reps as possible).[1][2]

People use it to gain muscle and strength during the first phase of lifting, since a more muscular physique is a common aesthetic goal. T Nation contributors recommend it to newcomers as a way to learn basic movements safely,[3] and describe it as hitting every primary movement pattern: vertical and horizontal push and pull, squat and deadlift.[4] One contributor suggests newcomers do the last set to failure, three exercises per day.[5]

Beginners who recommend it often pair it with eating in a surplus or a calorie target tailored to fat loss plus muscle gain, depending on the person.[6] A looksmax.org thread presents a spin-off, SkullStrength DUP, which adds daily undulating periodization to the Greyskull framework on the grounds that linear progression leads many lifters to plateaus.[1] No published trials have tested Greyskull LP specifically.

paras: Greyskull LP is a low-frequency, full-body routine with a few compound lifts per session and a final AMRAP set on main lifts.[1][2] Because the target weight increases session to session, it is called a linear progression.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and lifting communities
paras: T Nation members list it with Starting Strength as a beginner option,[3] suggest it as a base program with optional accessory work,[7] and describe it as a way to prepare for a long-term strength goal such as a 315 lb squat.[8] One poster says he gave the program to a friend.[9] The looksmax.org SkullStrength DUP thread calls it popular and proven and proposes undulating periodization once linear progress ends, while a reply says the poster dislikes only training three days a week.[1]

The SkullStrength author notes that linear progression with a few compound movements gets most lifters only so far before they hit a plateau on three sets of five.[1] Contributors also describe moving to templates with more volume as lifters pass the beginner phase.[5]

lore.intro: Greyskull LP appears in lifting and looksmaxxing forums as a recommended starting program.[1][3]

claims.claim: It is a good beginner program that teaches the big lifts
It protects bone density by covering every movement pattern
